newsitem.title: ISRAEL: SOCCER-ISRAEL RECALL STRIKER HARAZI FOR RUSSIA GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ISRAEL RECALL STRIKER HARAZI FOR RUSSIA GAME.

text.p: Striker Ronnen Harazi was recalled to the Israeli squad on Sunday for their World Cup qualifier against Moscow after six months out with an ankle injury.
Harazi, who has scored 19 goals in his 36 appearances in national colours, had been out of action since the 2-0 loss to Cyprus in a group 5 qualifying match in Limassol last November.

Israel coach Shlomo Scharf recalled him for the match in Moscow on June 8 after Harazi made his first appearance in newly-crowned champions Betar Jerusalem's starting line-up since regaining full fitness following an operation on his ankle.
Harazi's team mate Eli Ohana is expected to wear the captain's armband in place of Tal Banin, who is suspended for one match.
Also named in the 20-man squad are three of the five players who were suspended a day before the game against Cyprus in Tel Aviv last month after breaking a team curfew.

The three are Avi Nimni, Felix Halfon and David Amsalem. Of the other two, Haim Revivo, a midfielder for Spain's Celta Vigo, will be included only if he can get to a training camp before Israel leave for Moscow on June 4.
The fifth suspended player, former captain Nir Klinger, announced his retirement from international soccer immediately after being suspended.
Goalkeepers: Rafi Cohen (Hapoel Haifa), Itzik Kornfein (Betar Jerusalem).

Defenders: Moshe Glam (Maccabi Haifa), Amir Shelah (Maccabi Tel Aviv), Alon Harazi (Maccabi Haifa), Assi Domb (Betar Jerusalem), David Amsalem (Betar Jerusalem), Felix Halfon (Hapoel Tel Aviv), Arik Bennado (Maccabi Haifa).
Midfielders: Eyal Berkowitz (Southampton), Reuven Atar (Maccabi Haifa), Avi Nimni (Maccabi Tel Aviv), Itzik Zohar (Betar Jerusalem), Ran Ben-Shimon (Hapoel Haifa), Avishai Janno (Maccabi Haifa).
Strikers: Ronnen Harazi (Betar Jerusalem), Eli Ohana (Betar Jerusalem, captain), Alon Mizrahi (Bnei Yehuda), Ronnie Rosenthal (Tottenham Hotspur), Shai Holtzman (Hapoel Beersheba).
